# Teranode absences: what each implementation does not carry, and a ruling for each (#96)

**Generated by `tools/teranode_absences.py` from `corpus/teranode/absences.json` (#96); never edited by hand.** [D] 2026-10-14; the rulings [M] 2026-10-15. Teranode v0.16.0 `4edb60a4` against bitcoin-sv v1.2.3 `6504a3af` (`docs/PROVENANCE.md` section 1a). Every present side is cited at file and line [SRC]; every absent side is a directory listed at the tag and the searches that found nothing, or only the hits named, each quoted as the command that reproduces it in a clone of the repository (`<teranode clone>`, `<bitcoin-sv clone>`: `teranode.clone` and `reference.clone` of `docs/PROVENANCE.md` section 1a) [SRC]. `tools/teranode_absences.py --verify` re-reads every citation, listing and search at the pins. The module map of #87 (`corpus/teranode/map.json`, which lands with #87) keys the same surfaces by its `id`; each absence here carries that `id` (`map_id`) and #87's issue word in the #87 column, and every map row whose mechanism is `absent` has a row here.

**The rulings are the maintainers', by the rule of 2026-10-15.** The maintainers ruled 19 of 19 rows by one rule (the maintainers' ruling of 2026-10-15 between 22:10 and 22:19 UTC; the record docs/records/20261015-223120-s8-96-rulings-s3.md, section 1):

> A row is GAP when a transaction-level client depends on the surface: a wallet behavior, a broadcaster or payment service, or a status word of #67 or an event of #84 that such a client consumes.
> A row is DROPPED when only an operator, a peer or a relay encoding depends on it, OR when the information reaches such a client by another carrier of the same implementation, named on the row as its counterpart: the carrier changed, not the promise.
> A reference-lacks row is NEW.
> The rule is applied to every row, now and at every later release; a row's proposal is a reading of its dependents and its counterpart, and the rule decides.

The rows whose ruling differs from the proposal: [`tl.soft-freeze`](#tlsoft-freeze), proposed `dropped`, ruled `gap`: its dependent is the tip a node follows. The reference: a block whose input spends a consensus-frozen output fails `CheckInputs` with `REJECT_SOFT_CONSENSUS_FREEZE` and is soft frozen for `-softconsensusfreezeduration` blocks (a setting, default 3, `src/validation.h:219`; 0 holds it indefinitely, `src/init.cpp:1214-1221`) (`src/validation.cpp:3402-3406`), and a soft-frozen block cannot join the best chain until it has enough descendant blocks to pass the threshold (`src/block_index.h:283-285`), all at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af` [SRC]. Teranode: the alert service freezes the output in the UTXO store (row rl.alert-service; `AddToConsensusBlacklist`, `services/alert/node.go:274`, calling `FreezeUTXOs` at :346, which sets the spending id to FF...FF, `stores/utxo/aerospike/alert_system.go:71-77`); the store's spend refuses a frozen output with `ERR_UTXO_FROZEN` (`stores/utxo/aerospike/spend.go:1103-1107`); the validator returns the refusal as a processing error (`services/validator/Validator.go:1248`), which subtree validation does not read as an invalid transaction (`errors.Is` matches by code, `errors/errors.go:181`; `services/subtreevalidation/check_block_subtrees.go:1410`, :1474-1475), so block validation returns it without accepting the block and without storing it invalid (`services/blockvalidation/BlockValidation.go:2123`, :2161), all at Teranode `4edb60a4` [SRC, the subtree-validation path; the legacy-sync path not traced]. So the two alert-following nodes hold the same tip while the reference's hold lasts and can hold different tips once it lapses, for as long as the frozen spend's branch leads on the reference [D]. #94's measured leg is where it is witnessed. Every other row is ruled as proposed.

Nothing on this page is a rule of validity: the rows are surfaces, events and policies; an absence of a notification, a pool or a transport is node behavior, and a policy setting is never consensus.

| word | ruling |
|---|---|
| `dropped` | dropped on purpose |
| `pending` | pending in Teranode |
| `gap` | a gap a client will feel |
| `new` | new behavior the reference never had |

## Corrections to the issues' source lines [SRC]

- **#96's Source line, "ZMQ in 1 Go file".** At the tag no Go file uses ZeroMQ. A case-insensitive substring search for `zmq` over the Go files returns one file, services/legacy/bsvec/secp256k1.go, whose hit is inside base64 data (line 10, the precomputed points blob); the word-bounded search returns go.mod's two indirect requirements (go.mod:113-114), their go.sum checksums and three SV-node test configurations under test/config/, none of them Go code. The search: `git -C <teranode clone> grep -il 'zmq' 4edb60a4 -- '*.go'` returns 1 file: `services/legacy/bsvec/secp256k1.go`.
- **#96's and #87's Source lines, "model/Block.go:101 (subtrees)".** At the tag the Block struct's `Subtrees` field (the subtree roots) is model/Block.go:100 and `SubtreeSlices` (the subtrees themselves, not serialized) is :101; the ledger cites :100-101. The citation: `model/Block.go:100-101` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

## What Teranode does not carry

### tl.dsdetected

**The `dsdetected` P2P message and its webhook.** not carried by Teranode; the #87 row: `double-spend-notify` (event surface).

A peer announces a block (or blocks) observed to contain an attempt to double-spend some UTXOs; the reference checks the message, accepts the headers, updates the blocks' status, relays it to its other peers and posts it to the configured webhook.

Present [SRC]:

- `src/protocol.h:406-410` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the message and its meaning (at `extern const char* const DSDETECTED;`)
- `src/net/net_processing.cpp:4826-4827` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the dispatch (at `NetMsgType::DSDETECTED`)
- `src/net/net_processing.cpp:4648` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the blocks' status updated (at `UpdateBlockStatus(msg)`)
- `src/net/net_processing.cpp:4657-4665` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the relay to every other peer (at `NetMsgType::DSDETECTED, msg`)
- `src/net/net_processing.cpp:4668-4676` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the webhook post (at `CreateForDoubleSpendDetectedWebhook`)
- `src/init.cpp:1637` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the webhook's setting (at `-dsdetectedwebhookurl`)

Absent [SRC]: `git -C <teranode clone> ls-tree --name-only 4edb60a4 services/` (the listing below); then

- `git -C <teranode clone> grep -il 'dsdetected' 4edb60a4` returns no file

The other side's nearest: Teranode refuses the second spend at validation (`ErrTxInvalidDoubleSpend` and `ErrTxConflicting`, errors/Error_types.go:60-64; HTTP 409 on the propagation surface, services/propagation/Server.go:768-773) and marks the losing transaction `conflicting` in the UTXO store (row rl.conflicting-record); no message tells a peer or a service that a block carrying a double spend was seen.
[SRC] `errors/Error_types.go:60-64` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; `services/propagation/Server.go:768-773` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

What depends on it today:

- a service registered at `-dsdetectedwebhookurl` (a payment processor or a broadcaster watching for competing blocks) [D]
- the reference's peers, which relay the message onward
- #67's derived status `conflictedByMinedSpend`: DESIGN-S6 section 3 row 6 names the double-spend notification (S7's #80) as one of the node's own words for it
- #80's deliverable (the dsdetected format, the webhook delivery)

**Proposed ruling [D]: `gap`, a gap a client will feel.** A service that learns of a double spend in a competing block from the reference's webhook learns nothing from Teranode: no message, no webhook, no event, and the derived status `conflictedByMinedSpend` then has only the chain read to stand on. The status itself remains derivable (it is a chain fact), so what breaks is the push, the timing a service relies on, not the state.

**The maintainers' ruling:** `gap` (2026-10-15, by the maintainers' rule).

**Section 3** (#140): beyond the protocol: SV-node's conveniences and its operator or peer surfaces, which Teranode does not carry by design; a client builds on section 2 instead.

**The design:** Teranode settles a double spend inside the UTXO store, not by announcement: a double spend is rejected outright during normal transaction validation, and one that arrives inside a block with valid proof of work is saved and marked `conflicting`, with its children, so that the chain of most work decides and a reorganization can be handled consistently (its double-spend design page). A loose double spend's refusal is gossiped to peers with its reason (row rl.rejected-tx-gossip); a block is not announced as carrying one. [LIT] `docs/topics/architecture/understandingDoubleSpends.md:57-62` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `stores/utxo/Interface.go:537-541` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `services/propagation/Server.go:768-773` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `services/p2p/message_types.go:126-139` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

**A client:** A client reads a double spend in a competing block the way the whitepaper's reader does, by headers and proofs: it re-asks its proof when the tip moves; on the reference the `dsdetected` webhook, where an operator configured one, is a hint that may arrive sooner, never the evidence.

**Measured, the reference** [X]: a peer's `dsdetected` message (685 bytes) valid at B, relayed to A only and posted to B's webhook; valid at A, relayed to A's other peer only and posted to A's webhook; both bodies 1896 bytes, equal to the model's; the repeat answered by the duplicate cache with no relay and no post (`chaincheck --dsnt`: 47 checks agree, 0 witnesses) (record `docs/records/20261015-165715-s7-80-double-spend-s1.md`; receipt `docs/records/20261015-165715-s7-80-double-spend-s1.json`; receipt `corpus/p2p/2026-10-15-double-spend-two-node.receipt.json`).

**Measured, Teranode** [M]: the second spend of an accepted output refused (`mempool/accepted-spend-conflict`: RPC code -25, the verdict agree with the reference's `txn-mempool-conflict`, check 5); no `dsdetected` message or webhook exists to observe (the row's searches, [SRC]); the 409 on the propagation surface and the rejected-transaction gossip stand as a reading at the pin (#80's record, section 5 of docs/CONFORMANCE-DOUBLE-SPEND.md), not yet a run (record `docs/records/20261016-001926-s8-97-contract-check5-s4b.md`; receipt `docs/records/20261016-001926-s6-66-cut2-second-oracle-s3.json`).

The view it breaks:

- #67: `conflictedByMinedSpend` (spec/status-views.md, the row; the ProvenTxReqStatus column's partial `doubleSpend`) ([page](status-views.md))
- #84: the double-spend notification beside #84's removal events (#80 writes it; #84's vocabulary maps it)

### tl.ds-attempt-callback

**The double-spend attempt handler and its callback to the transaction's declared endpoint.** not carried by Teranode; the #87 row: `double-spend-notify` (conflicts).

When a transaction arrives that double-spends an input of a transaction the reference already holds, the reference's handler can call back the endpoint the original transaction declared in its notification output, at a level the operator sets (none, standard transactions only, all), with fast and slow callback queues, a slow-endpoint rate limit and a time-limited blacklist.

Present [SRC]:

- `src/double_spend/dsattempt_handler.h:34` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the handler (at `class DSAttemptHandler final`)
- `src/double_spend/dsattempt_handler.h:75` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: a detected attempt submitted (at `HandleDoubleSpend`)
- `src/double_spend/dsattempt_handler.h:122` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the notification sent (at `SendNotification`)
- `src/double_spend/dscallback_msg.h:20` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the callback message carried in the output (at `class DSCallbackMsg`)
- `src/init.cpp:1576-1578` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the operator's level (at `-dsnotifylevel`)
- `src/double_spend/dsattempt_handler.h:48-54` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the blacklist size, the fast and slow thread pools and the slow-endpoint rate limit (at `DEFAULT_DS_ENDPOINT_BLACKLIST_SIZE`)
- `src/double_spend/dsattempt_handler.h:193-194` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the time-limited blacklist of callback servers (at `TimeLimitedBlacklist`)

Absent [SRC]: `git -C <teranode clone> ls-tree --name-only 4edb60a4 services/` (the listing below); then

- `git -C <teranode clone> grep -il 'dsattempt' 4edb60a4` returns no file
- `git -C <teranode clone> grep -il 'dscallback' 4edb60a4` returns no file
- `git -C <teranode clone> grep -il 'dsendpoint' 4edb60a4` returns no file
- `git -C <teranode clone> grep -il 'dsnt' 4edb60a4` returns no file

The other side's nearest: The attempt is refused at validation with HTTP 409 (services/propagation/Server.go:768-773); the original transaction's submitter is not told; the rejection, with its reason, is gossiped to peers on the rejected-transaction topic (row rl.rejected-tx-gossip), never to the original transaction's declared endpoint.
[SRC] `services/propagation/Server.go:768-773` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

What depends on it today:

- a wallet that declares a callback endpoint in a transaction's output to hear of attempts against its inputs [D]
- Arcade's word `DOUBLE_SPEND_ATTEMPTED` (#67's Arcade vocabulary, lean/BsvChain/Views/Status.lean:38) when its producer reads a node's attempt signal [D]
- #80's deliverable (the detector's events, the callback message, the webhook rules)

**Proposed ruling [D]: `gap`, a gap a client will feel.** The callback is addressed by the transaction itself, so the client that wrote the endpoint is the one that stops hearing; nothing on Teranode's surfaces carries an attempt against someone else's pending transaction to that transaction's owner.

**The maintainers' ruling:** `gap` (2026-10-15, by the maintainers' rule).

**Section 3** (#140): beyond the protocol: SV-node's conveniences and its operator or peer surfaces, which Teranode does not carry by design; a client builds on section 2 instead.

**The design:** Teranode scales horizontally, to over a million transactions a second, and it does so with no traditional mempool: a transaction is validated and organized into subtrees as it arrives, and continuous validation and subtree creation replaces mempool functionality (its system design's comparison table). With no pool to hold a contested transaction, a double spend is settled where the outputs live, at the UTXO store: the second spend of an output is refused at validation (HTTP 409 on the propagation surface), and the refusal is gossiped to peers with its reason on the rejected-transaction topic (row rl.rejected-tx-gossip). The outcome is a verdict to the submitter, not a callback to an endpoint the earlier transaction declared. [LIT] `docs/topics/architecture/teranode-overall-system-design.md:174` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `services/propagation/Server.go:768-773` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `services/p2p/message_types.go:126-139` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

**A client:** A client that must know whether its spend stands watches its own proof: a valid merkle proof against the active header settles it, and a refusal on broadcast tells the submitter of the later spend at once; nothing is addressed to an endpoint in the transaction's own output.

**Measured, the reference** [X]: the attempt handler took each refused double spend, checked its input and called back the declared endpoint (a query and a submit for E1, the query alone for E2, nothing for the blacklisted E3), each as the model predicts (`chaincheck --dsnt`) (record `docs/records/20261015-165715-s7-80-double-spend-s1.md`; receipt `docs/records/20261015-165715-s7-80-double-spend-s1.json`).

**Measured, Teranode** [M]: the double spend refused at intake (`mempool/accepted-spend-conflict`: RPC code -25, agree, check 5); no callback surface exists to observe (the row's searches, [SRC]) (record `docs/records/20261016-001926-s8-97-contract-check5-s4b.md`; receipt `docs/records/20261016-001926-s6-66-cut2-second-oracle-s3.json`).

The view it breaks:

- #67: the Arcade word `DOUBLE_SPEND_ATTEMPTED` (#67's Arcade vocabulary, lean/BsvChain/Views/Status.lean:38; spec/status-views.md maps no derived status to it): no node-side producer on Teranode ([page](../lean/BsvChain/Views/Status.lean))
- #84: the double-spend attempt event (#80's detector events, mapped through #84's vocabulary)

### tl.zmq-announce

**The ZMQ announcement topics: hashblock, rawblock, hashtx, rawtx and their `2` variants.** not carried by Teranode; the #87 row: `event-zmq` (event surface).

The reference publishes, on ZeroMQ sockets the operator names, every new block and every transaction accepted (hash or raw), the `2` variants on a separate topic prefix.

Present [SRC]:

- `src/zmq/zmqnotificationinterface.cpp:59-80` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the topic factories (at `factories["pubhashblock"]`)
- `src/zmq/zmqpublishnotifier.cpp:22-36` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the topic names (at `MSG_HASHBLOCK = "hashblock"`)
- `src/init.cpp:886-913` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: the settings (at `-zmqpubhashblock=<address>`)

Absent [SRC]: `git -C <teranode clone> ls-tree --name-only 4edb60a4 services/` (the listing below); then

- `git -C <teranode clone> grep -ilw 'zmq\|zeromq' 4edb60a4` returns 5 files: `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `test/config/svnode-1.conf`, `test/config/svnode-2.conf`, `test/config/svnode-3.conf` (go.mod:113-114 are indirect requirements and go.sum holds their checksums; the three files are SV-node configurations for Teranode's tests; no Go file (see the correction above))

The other side's nearest: Blocks are announced on the P2P service's websocket (row rl.websocket; type `block`, services/p2p/server_helpers.go:111; `subtree`, :287) and on the Kafka block topics (settings/settings.go:154, :161); accepted transactions move between services on the Kafka validator and txmeta topics (:151-152), which #97 names as what an application on Teranode reads instead of ZMQ.
[SRC] `services/p2p/server_helpers.go:111` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; `settings/settings.go:151-161` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

What depends on it today:

- a subscriber to the reference's block and transaction topics (an indexer, a broadcaster, a wallet backend) [D]
- #84's vocabulary (`pubhashtx`, `pubrawtx`, `pubhashtx2`, `pubrawtx2` named in #84's Source)

**Proposed ruling [D]: `dropped`, dropped on purpose.** Every announcement has a Teranode carrier (the websocket for blocks and subtrees, Kafka for blocks and transactions) and no derived status of #67 reads an announcement; a subscriber moves to another transport and #97 writes its contract. What is lost is the transport, not the information. By the maintainers' rule the row is DROPPED by its carrier clause: the information reaches the subscriber by another Teranode carrier, the counterpart (row rl.websocket and the Kafka topics).

**The maintainers' ruling:** `dropped` (2026-10-15, by the maintainers' rule).

**Section 3** (#140): beyond the protocol: SV-node's conveniences and its operator or peer surfaces, which Teranode does not carry by design; a client builds on section 2 instead.

**The design:** Teranode's services exchange blocks and transactions over Kafka topics, and its Asset Service offers clients a WebSocket interface for real-time notifications when new subtrees and blocks are added; block announcements ride those carriers. [LIT] `docs/topics/services/assetServer.md:67` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `services/p2p/server_helpers.go:111` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `settings/settings.go:151-161` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

**A client:** A client subscribes to tips through whichever push its node offers (`hashblock` over ZMQ on the reference, the `block` notification over the WebSocket on Teranode) and treats each as a hint to re-ask its proofs, never as evidence.

### tl.zmq-removal

**The ZMQ removal topics with reasons: discardedfrommempool and removedfrommempoolblock.** not carried by Teranode; the #87 row: `event-zmq` (event surface).

The reference publishes each transaction leaving its pool with the reason (and, for a conflict, the transaction it conflicted with), and each transaction removed because a block included it or a conflicting spend.

Present [SRC]:

- `src/zmq/zmqnotificationinterface.cpp:266` at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af`: removal by a block (at `NotifyRemovedFromMempoolBlock(txid, reason)`)

- the tip a node follows, and with it the block a transaction-level client reads its transaction in: the reference and Teranode, both following the alerts, hold the same tip while the reference holds a frozen spend's block out of its best chain (until the block has `-softconsensusfreezeduration` child blocks, a setting, default 3, `src/validation.h:219` at `6504a3af`) and can hold different tips once that hold lapses, Teranode refusing the block (the maintainers' ruling, 2026-10-15; the mechanism [SRC] in `ruling.owner_reason`) [D]

**Proposed ruling [D]: `dropped`, dropped on purpose.** No view of #67 or event of #84 reads the freeze; it moves chain selection only for a block that spends a consensus-frozen output, an alert-system case whose Teranode handling is #94's and #93's to read [D]. No Teranode source at the tag names it as planned, so `pending` has no citation; the maintainers may read it as `gap` once #94 reads Teranode's frozen-block path. The duration is a setting.

**The maintainers' ruling:** `gap` (2026-10-15, by the maintainers' rule). It differs from the proposal: its dependent is the tip a node follows. The reference: a block whose input spends a consensus-frozen output fails `CheckInputs` with `REJECT_SOFT_CONSENSUS_FREEZE` and is soft frozen for `-softconsensusfreezeduration` blocks (a setting, default 3, `src/validation.h:219`; 0 holds it indefinitely, `src/init.cpp:1214-1221`) (`src/validation.cpp:3402-3406`), and a soft-frozen block cannot join the best chain until it has enough descendant blocks to pass the threshold (`src/block_index.h:283-285`), all at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af` [SRC]. Teranode: the alert service freezes the output in the UTXO store (row rl.alert-service; `AddToConsensusBlacklist`, `services/alert/node.go:274`, calling `FreezeUTXOs` at :346, which sets the spending id to FF...FF, `stores/utxo/aerospike/alert_system.go:71-77`); the store's spend refuses a frozen output with `ERR_UTXO_FROZEN` (`stores/utxo/aerospike/spend.go:1103-1107`); the validator returns the refusal as a processing error (`services/validator/Validator.go:1248`), which subtree validation does not read as an invalid transaction (`errors.Is` matches by code, `errors/errors.go:181`; `services/subtreevalidation/check_block_subtrees.go:1410`, :1474-1475), so block validation returns it without accepting the block and without storing it invalid (`services/blockvalidation/BlockValidation.go:2123`, :2161), all at Teranode `4edb60a4` [SRC, the subtree-validation path; the legacy-sync path not traced]. So the two alert-following nodes hold the same tip while the reference's hold lasts and can hold different tips once it lapses, for as long as the frozen spend's branch leads on the reference [D]. #94's measured leg is where it is witnessed.

**Section 3** (#140): beyond the protocol: SV-node's conveniences and its operator or peer surfaces, which Teranode does not carry by design; a client builds on section 2 instead.

**The design:** Teranode carries the alert system inside the node (row rl.alert-service): an alert freezes the output in the UTXO store, for network security and compliance purposes as its glossary says, so the store's spend refuses the frozen output wherever the spend is made, at intake and inside a block alike, and there is no block-level hold to release. [LIT] `docs/references/glossary.md:3` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [LIT] `docs/references/services/alert_reference.md:190` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `services/alert/node.go:346` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `stores/utxo/aerospike/spend.go:1103-1107` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; [SRC] `stores/utxo/sql/sql.go:2434-2435` at Teranode `4edb60a4`.

**A client:** A client never builds on a spend of an output it knows to be frozen, and treats a block that carries one by depth on the chain its node follows: the reference holds such a block out of its best chain for `-softconsensusfreezeduration` blocks (a setting, default 3) and Teranode's store refuses its spend, so a proof into that block is evidence only once the block is on the active chain at the client's depth.

**Measured, the reference** [M]: at the default duration (the setting unset, 3): block A at 103, spending a consensus-blacklisted output, answered `bad-txns-inputs-frozen` by `submitblock` and held: `getblock` confirmations -1 with the soft consensus freeze flag set, `getchaintips` its branch `valid-headers`, the tip at 102; three coinbase-only blocks on A each answered `inconclusive` with the tip held at 102; at the fourth (107) the chain through A activated, the tip A+4, A's confirmations 5, the frozen output spent; with `softconsensusfreezeduration=0` the tip stayed at 102 through five blocks on A and the output stayed unspent (tools/soft_freeze_probe.py, two fresh regtest instances; one run of record, an earlier run discarded for a projection key collision, record section 5) (record `docs/records/20261016-172953-s8-140-node-client-contract-s3.md`; receipt `docs/records/20261016-173411-s8-140-soft-freeze-reference-s3.json`).

**Measured, Teranode** [M]: on the cut 2 road (the legacy recipe, under the quarantine rule, `ORACLE_ROWS` the two frozen rows, the contract's freeze call at three parameters): the freeze accepted (`frozen` true: the freeze RPC answered without error, `harness/src/scenarios/road.rs:1805-1820`; the handler sets the store's flag, `services/rpc/handlers.go:2725`), and the block spending the frozen output refused on the bridge's wire with reject code 16 (`REJECT_INVALID`, 0x10 at bitcoin-sv `6504a3af` `src/consensus/validation.h:15`, the value Teranode sends being go-wire's `RejectInvalid RejectCode = 0x10`, `msg_reject.go:21` in go-wire v1.2.11, the version Teranode's `go.mod` requires at `4edb60a4`, the bridge's code, with the text "block rejected", for any block it refuses outside a transient local error, [SRC] `services/legacy/netsync/manager.go:2099-2100` at Teranode `4edb60a4`; the code does not name the freeze, whose refusal is the reading of the store's spend above; `frozen/block`: status rejected, verdict agree with the reference's refusal of the same block; `availability/precedes-frozen`: refused too, agreeing with the reference's `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent`); blocks built on the refused block were not driven on Teranode (the road delivers one block per row), so the half after the reference's hold lapses is owed to #94's measured leg (record `docs/records/20261016-172953-s8-140-node-client-contract-s3.md`; receipt `docs/records/20261016-173953-s6-66-cut2-second-oracle-s3.json`).

The view it breaks:

- #67: `minedActive h` and `onStaleBranch` [D] (a reading, the maintainers' ruling of 2026-10-15) for a transaction in a block that spends a consensus-frozen output or in a block built on it: on the reference it reads `onStaleBranch` while the block is held out of selection and `minedActive h` once it unfreezes; on Teranode, whose UTXO store refuses the frozen spend, it never reads `minedActive` on that branch; #94's measured leg is the witness, not yet run ([page](status-views.md))
